article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Gelato #45 × White Diesel × High Octane × Jet Fuel
Breeder: Compound Genetics
THC Content: 20–25%
CBD Content: Low, generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , myrcene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Peppermint, menthol, earth, diesels
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: 400–500 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500–600 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

The Menthol takes a familiar modern cannabis formula— Gelato sweetness layered over aggressive fuel genetics—and pushes it in an unexpectedly cold direction. Compound Genetics created the cultivar from Gelato #45 and a complex combination of White Diesel, High Octane, and Jet Fuel G6, producing chunky frost-covered flowers with a fragrance the breeder compares to a minty Tiger Balm sundae. Behind the cooling first impression sit gasoline, pepper, cream, damp earth, and chemical sharpness, making the weed considerably more complicated than the name suggests. It also became one of Compound Genetics’ most influential breeding plants, contributing to well-known descendants including Khalifa Mints, Pink Certz , Eye Candy, and numerous later Menthol-series hybrids.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder documents the lineage as Gelato #45 × [White Diesel × (High Octane × Jet Fuel G6)]. Although shortened descriptions sometimes list all four cultivars as if they contributed equally, the nested pedigree better explains how the genetics were assembled. Gelato #45 forms one side of the cross, while White Diesel is combined with a High Octane and Jet Fuel G6 hybrid on the other. That arrangement concentrates several generations of fuel-oriented marijuana beneath a sweeter, resin-heavy Gelato parent.

Gelato #45 supplies density, visual frost, creamy sweetness, and the polished flower structure associated with modern California cannabis. White Diesel adds pungent fuel and sharper herbal character, while High Octane contributes OG-derived weight and deep gasoline notes. Jet Fuel G6 reinforces the chemical side with additional Diesel ancestry and vigorous growth. Compound’s own description summarizes the finished cultivar as a mixture of Gelato #45, White Diesel, High Octane, and Jet Fuel G6 and emphasizes its cool peppermint-menthol terpene character.

The importance of the genetics becomes even clearer in Compound’s later breeding work. The Menthol has been crossed into Apples & Bananas , Red Bullz, Jokerz #31 , Gastro Pop , Rose Gold Runtz , and numerous other lines. Compound specifically credits its Menthol collections with contributing strong yields, powdery-mildew resistance, gas-heavy aromatics, and suitability for greenhouse and field-scale cultivation. Few modern weed strains demonstrate breeding value as clearly as a parent that continues appearing throughout multiple generations of a breeder’s catalog.
Effects and Experience

The opening has more energy than the indica-leaning classification might suggest. An initial cerebral push can elevate mood quickly, encouraging conversation, creative thinking, or a heightened interest in whatever is happening around the consumer. Weedmaps describes the strain as an indica-leaning hybrid, while contemporary consumer profiles frequently mention an upbeat mental phase before the heavier physical effects take over.

That early brightness gradually gives way to a much calmer second half. Warm physical relaxation spreads through the body as the racing edge of the initial high subsides, creating a contrast that makes the cultivar suitable for late afternoon or evening use for many experienced consumers. At moderate amounts, the body feels loose without necessarily becoming immobile. Push the dose higher and the indica side becomes far more apparent, potentially turning a sociable beginning into a sleepy, deeply relaxed finish.

Potency should not be underestimated. Secondary cultivation records commonly place THC near 25%, while Compound itself describes the flowers as exceptionally powerful without publishing a universal cannabinoid number for the original cultivar. Actual potency depends on phenotype, lighting, harvest maturity, curing, and laboratory methodology. For consumers with lower THC tolerance, the combination of a quick cerebral rise and substantial later body effect makes conservative dosing sensible.
Medical Benefits

The Menthol’s two-stage experience may appeal to medical marijuana consumers looking for both mood elevation and physical relaxation. The more animated beginning can be attractive during periods of temporary stress, subdued mood, or mental fatigue, while the later heaviness may be preferable when physical tension or difficulty winding down becomes the greater concern. High-THC examples can also produce a pronounced alteration in how discomfort is perceived.

No controlled clinical research has established The Menthol itself as a treatment for insomnia, PTSD, anxiety, chronic pain, depression, or another medical disorder. Reports connecting the cultivar with such uses are based on consumer experience rather than strain-specific medical trials. Cannabinoid composition can also differ substantially between harvests carrying the same name.

Because the strain is generally THC dominant with little CBD, large doses may be counterproductive for people sensitive to THC. Anxiety, dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, or excessive sedation can occur. Medical consumers are better served by reviewing the laboratory analysis of the particular flower or extract rather than assuming every Menthol sample will produce identical effects.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The first aromatic impression explains the name immediately. Compound Genetics describes the cultivar as having cool peppermint and menthol terpenes and memorably compares the overall flavor with a minty Tiger Balm sundae. The cooling sensation is surrounded by earth, black pepper, diesel fuel, and chemical sharpness, while Gelato #45 contributes enough cream and sweetness to soften the edges.

Grinding the flower can deepen the fuel character. What initially smells like peppermint balm may begin revealing wet earth, peppercorn, gasoline, pine, and an almost medicinal eucalyptus-like edge. Weedmaps similarly records mint, spice, chemicals, diesel, and black pepper as characteristic parts of the aroma and flavor. The effect is closer to opening a jar of herbal cooling ointment beside a fuel can than eating a conventional mint dessert.

Terpene composition is not fixed. Contemporary samples have been associated with caryophyllene, myrcene, terpinolene, limonene, pinene, and linalool, but different growers can produce different dominant profiles. For that reason, the combination of cool mint, pepper, earth, and gas is a more dependable identifying feature than assigning one terpene as universally dominant.
Growing Information

The Menthol earned substantial breeding attention partly because of its agronomic traits. Compound Genetics describes its Menthol breeding family as capable of transmitting high yields, powdery-mildew resistance, distinctive terpenes, and relatively easy cultivation, including performance in greenhouses and field-scale environments. Those qualities make the genetics useful beyond boutique indoor production.

Indoor flowering is commonly placed around eight to nine weeks. Secondary cultivation references narrow the window to approximately 54–63 days and estimate indoor production around 400–500 g/m². Expect medium to vigorous growth with enough stretch to justify early canopy management. Topping, low-stress training, or a trellis can help distribute the plant’s productive branches beneath the strongest area of the lighting footprint. Resin development can become extremely heavy near maturity, producing the glistening white appearance highlighted by Compound Genetics.

Outdoor plants benefit from full sun, generous root volume, and good airflow through the second half of flowering. Production around 500–600 grams per plant has been cited under productive conditions, though such figures should be considered targets rather than guarantees. Compound’s continued use of The Menthol in greenhouse and field-oriented breeding projects is particularly notable, suggesting that vigor and mildew resistance were important enough to preserve across subsequent generations.
FAQ
What are the genetics of The Menthol?

Compound Genetics identifies the lineage as Gelato #45 × [White Diesel × (High Octane × Jet Fuel G6)]. The combination joins Gelato-derived density and sweetness with multiple fuel-heavy cannabis lines.
Is The Menthol an indica or sativa?
It is generally classified as an indica-leaning hybrid. The effects can initially feel cerebral and uplifting before gradually moving toward stronger physical relaxation.
How much THC does The Menthol have?

Compound does not publish one universal breeder THC specification for the original cultivar. Contemporary references commonly place examples around 20–25% or higher, but actual laboratory results vary by phenotype and cultivation conditions.
What does The Menthol strain taste like?

Peppermint and cooling menthol are the signature flavors, accompanied by black pepper, earth, diesel, chemical gas, herbs, and creamy Gelato sweetness. Compound describes the terpene expression as distinctly peppermint-menthol in character.
How long does The Menthol take to flower?

Approximately eight to nine weeks is a useful indoor reference, with secondary cultivation specifications commonly placing maturity around 54–63 days. Outdoor harvest generally falls around early to mid-autumn depending on climate and latitude.
Final Thoughts on The Menthol

The Menthol demonstrates why Compound Genetics has returned to these genetics repeatedly rather than treating the cultivar as a one-time release. Gelato #45 supplies resin, density, and creamy sweetness, while White Diesel, High Octane, and Jet Fuel G6 build an unusually deep fuel foundation. From that combination emerges the trait that made the strain famous: a cold peppermint and herbal sensation layered over earth, pepper, chemicals, and gasoline.

Its influence may ultimately be as important as the original weed itself. Khalifa Mints, Pink Certz, Eye Candy, A.B. Parfait, Puffinz, Polar Pop, and numerous other Compound projects carry The Menthol in their ancestry, demonstrating how effectively it passes along resin, vigor, gas, and unusual terpene expression. For consumers, it offers a strong cerebral-to-physical progression and a flavor unlike ordinary mint cannabis. For growers and breeders, its combination of frost, production potential, disease resistance, and distinctive cool gas profile explains why The Menthol became one of Compound Genetics’ foundational modern cultivars.
